title: Projecting Breast Cancer Test Data onto the 1D Logit Score and Unscaling Weights
description: Compute decision_function logits z_test and probabilities p_test for the breast cancer test set, plot them on the sigmoid curve, and convert coefficients from standardized space back to original feature units.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Load the breast cancer dataset and split it using the supplied ratio with `stratify=y`. Fit `pipe` (`StandardScaler` + `LogisticRegression`) and compute `z_test = pipe.decision_function(X_test)` and `p_test = pipe.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]`.
Build `z_grid` with the supplied point count spanning `[z_min - padding, z_max + padding]`. Plot the sigmoid curve `(z_grid, sig_grid)` and overlay `(z_test, y_test + jitter)` and `(z_test, p_test)`.

Extract `logreg = pipe.named_steps["logreg"]` and `scaler = pipe.named_steps["scaler"]`, pull out `theta0_std = logreg.intercept_.item()` and `theta_std = logreg.coef_.ravel()`, and print their values in standardized space.

Look at lines 70-75: substitute `x_std = (x - scaler.mean_) / scaler.scale_` into `theta0_std + theta_std @ x_std`. This divides each weight by `scaler.scale_` (`theta_orig = theta_std / scaler.scale_`). It shifts the intercept by `-np.sum(theta_std * scaler.mean_ / scaler.scale_)`.

steps.question: Why is the L2 norm of the weights so much larger in original feature units (`‖θ‖₂ = 169.364182`) than in standardized units (`‖θ‖₂ = 3.518419`)?
steps.answer: Because dividing `theta_std` by `scaler.scale_` on line 74 multiplies weights for tiny-scale features (such as `fractal dimension error` and `concave points error`) by large factors.

steps.description: Compute `theta_orig` and `theta0_orig` (`34.628168`), print their summary statistics, and assemble the full feature log-odds equation `equation_orig`.
